title: Colossians 3:12–17
context: The new self’s wardrobe: as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, believers clothe themselves in Christlike virtues, forgive as the Lord has forgiven, bind everything with love, let Christ’s peace rule the one body, let His word dwell richly, and do all in Jesus’ name with thanksgiving.

voices.heading: Voices from both camps
voices.intro: What earlier interpreters on each side wrote about Colossians 3:12–17.
voices.note: Quotations lightly abridged for length; wording follows standard English translations of the sources named.

arminian.quote: All who are thus renewed are elected of God, holy, and therefore the more beloved of him. Holiness is the consequence of their election, and God's superior love, of their holiness. Forbearing one another - If anything is now wrong. And forgiving one another - What is past.
arminian.source: Explanatory Notes upon the New Testament (on Col 3:12–17)

reformed.quote: The rendering that has been given by others, "super omnia haec," (above all these things,) instead of insuper, (over and above,) is, in my opinion, meagre. It would be more suitable to render it, Before all these things. I have chosen, however, the more ordinary signification of the word epi.

verses.text: Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance;
verses.arminianNotes:
“Put on therefore” continues the clothing metaphor. Identity phrases—“God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved”—describe the people in Christ before listing virtues. Arminian readers often hear corporate or conditional election accents: God chooses the people found in Christ, or chooses according to foreseen faith, while still naming them holy and dearly loved.

Chosenness motivates compassion, not pride. Grace that set them in the beloved community also enables the virtues they must actively wear.
verses.reformedNotes:
Indicative first: they are God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved—language of electing love and consecration. Imperatives of virtue flow from that prior grace.

Unconditional election in Christ grounds the “put on.” Compassion and patience are not ladders into chosenness but the fitting dress of those the Father has set apart in love.
verses.keyContrast: Both take “chosen ones, holy and beloved” as grace-identity that fuels virtue. Arminians typically accent corporate election in Christ and/or conditional election tied to faith, with chosenness describing the believing people; Reformed commentators often accent God’s unconditional election of particular persons in Christ, with holiness and love as fruits of that prior choice.

verses.text: bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
verses.arminianNotes:
Bearing and forgiving answer complaints inside the body. The measure is the Lord’s forgiveness already received—so you also must forgive.

Grace that forgave them enables and obliges them to forgive. The must is sincere and serious; withholding forgiveness contradicts the mercy they freely received.
verses.reformedNotes:
Forgiveness is patterned on the Lord’s prior pardon. Community patience and release of complaints mirror gospel grace already given.

Those forgiven in Christ cannot treat grievances as ultimate. The Spirit forms a people whose forbearance displays the same mercy that justified them.
verses.keyContrast: Both make the Lord’s forgiveness the template and ground of mutual pardon. Arminians stress an obligation empowered by resistible-in-principle grace that believers must not refuse; Reformed Christians typically emphasize Spirit-wrought forgiveness as the necessary fruit of effectual grace already shown in Christ.

verses.text: Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.
verses.arminianNotes:
Love is the outer garment “above all these,” binding the virtues into perfect harmony. Without love, kindness and patience can become performance.

Enabling grace produces love that holds the community together. Believers are summoned to put it on deliberately as the bond of maturity.
verses.reformedNotes:
Love crowns the wardrobe and unifies the rest into mature wholeness. It is not vague sentiment but the binding grace of the new creation.

Love poured into hearts by the Spirit perfects the body’s harmony. Christlike charity is the elect’s distinguishing dress.

verses.text: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.
verses.arminianNotes:
Christ’s peace is to “rule”—to umpire—hearts called into one body. Thanksgiving seals the posture.

Grace calls them into shared peace they must welcome and not disrupt. Letting peace rule means yielding disputes to Christ’s verdict rather than self-will.
verses.reformedNotes:
The peace of Christ is appointed as heart-ruler for those called into one body. Gratitude is the fitting atmosphere of that calling.

Application: union with Christ and calling into one body are God’s work; the peace that rules is His gift administering the community under His lordship.

verses.text: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your heart to the Lord.
verses.arminianNotes:
Christ’s word is to dwell richly—saturating the community with teaching, admonition, and thankful song. Mutual ministry flows from a word-filled people.

Grace opens ears and hearts to Scripture; the church remains responsible to let that word lodge deeply and shape speech and praise.
verses.reformedNotes:
The word of Christ indwelling richly produces wise teaching, admonition, and grateful worship. Song is theology on the lips of the body.

Christ rules His church by His word. Rich dwelling is Spirit-given fullness that forms a wise, thankful people under Scripture’s authority.

verses.text: Whatever you do, in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
verses.arminianNotes:
All of life—word and deed—comes under Jesus’ name, with thanks to the Father through Him. No sacred/secular split excuses ungrateful speech or action.

Enabling grace makes whole-life discipleship possible. Doing all in Jesus’ name is a sincere call to represent Him consciously in every sphere.
verses.reformedNotes:
Comprehensive lordship: all in the name of the Lord Jesus, thanksgiving routed to the Father through the Son. Christ mediates both obedience and praise.

Providence and redemption place every act under Jesus’ authority. Gratitude through Him is the Christian’s constant liturgy of ordinary life.
